reviews.scopeMarkdown:
**Số từ bài gốc: 137 từ**, đếm bằng cách tách nguyên văn theo khoảng trắng; thiếu 13 từ so với mức tối thiểu 150 từ. Yêu cầu bài viết: 150–200 từ.
Phạm vi: Cô chỉ chấm Đề 1 em đã gõ; không chấm Đề 2 hoặc bản scan.
reviews.overall: Em cần sửa và nộp lại. Bài này em làm còn ẩu: chưa đủ độ dài, nhiều câu chưa có dấu chấm, thiếu giới từ ở Detail 1 và thiếu động từ chính ở câu cuối. Em còn dùng sai chủ thể của động từ thay đổi và bỏ mốc đỉnh quan trọng của France. Em đã chia được hai nhóm, nhưng phải hoàn chỉnh câu và trình bày đủ đặc điểm chính. Đi học là để ghi chép, hiểu và vận dụng lại kiến thức khi tự viết. Cô yêu cầu em tự sửa các chỗ đã đánh dấu, bổ sung dữ liệu cần thiết và đọc lại từng câu trước khi nộp.
reviews.dataGrouping: Detail 1 của em gồm Germany rồi Italy; Detail 2 gồm United Kingdom, France rồi Belgium. Cách chia này hợp lý theo thứ hạng cuối kỳ: Germany–Italy có tỷ lệ phần trăm cao hơn ba nước còn lại vào năm 2012. Cô giữ cả nhóm và thứ tự trình bày, bổ sung diễn biến nổi bật trong nhóm thứ hai; không gọi nhóm Germany–Italy là cao nhất suốt giai đoạn vì France đứng đầu năm 2004.

The line graph illustrates the percentage of women in parliament across five European countries from 2000 to 2012
Overall, it is clear that the percentages of female representatives in most nations experienced an upward trend, whereas Germany changed very little. By 2012, Italy become the country with the highest figure, while the UK stayed at the lowest poóitio

Regarding the remaining countries, the UK had the lowest figure at only 3% in 2000, but  rose steadily to 27% in 2012. France and Belgium also  an overall increase, starting at 25% and 17%, and ending the period at around 32% and 28% respectively

annotations.title: Chủ thể của động từ thay đổi chưa đúng
annotations.headerMarkdown: **C05 · Chủ thể của động từ thay đổi chưa đúng**
annotations.bodyMarkdown:
- Overview: “Germany changed very little” → “the figure for Germany changed very little”. “The figure” thay cho tỷ lệ phần trăm nữ nghị sĩ đã nêu ở vế trước.
- Đầu Detail 1: “Germany started highest at 33%” → “In 2000, around 33% of parliamentarians in Germany were women”. Câu mở nêu đủ đại lượng, nước, năm và đơn vị; phần tăng tiếp tục nói về tỷ lệ phần trăm ấy.
- Đầu Detail 2: “the UK had the lowest figure at only 3% in 2000, but  rose steadily to 27% in 2012” → “the percentage of female parliamentarians in the United Kingdom rose from 3% in 2000 to 28% in 2012”. Mức cuối kỳ xem thêm C08.

Tên nước đang làm chủ ngữ của “changed”, “started/rising” hoặc “rose”, trong khi tỷ lệ phần trăm nữ nghị sĩ mới thay đổi. “Rose” dùng chung chủ ngữ “the UK” với “had”: đây là sai đối tượng, không phải thiếu chủ ngữ. “Italy experienced a significant increase” có thể dùng theo cách Cô đã dạy khi đại lượng đã rõ. Khi đổi sang “The figure for Italy”, em dùng “that for Germany” để so sánh hai tỷ lệ phần trăm.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The line graph illustrates how female representation in parliament, expressed as a percentage, changed in five European countries from 2000 to 2012.

Overall, the percentage of female parliamentarians increased in all five countries, most markedly in the United Kingdom and least in Germany. Italy had the highest final figure, while the United Kingdom stayed lowest, jointly with Belgium in 2012.

To elaborate, in 2000, around 33% of parliamentarians in Germany were women, with a subsequent slight rise to 37% in 2012. The figure for Italy rose more substantially from 26% to nearly 40%, surpassing that for Germany in 2012.

Regarding the remaining countries, the percentage of female parliamentarians in the United Kingdom rose from 3% in 2000 to 28% in 2012. The figure for France increased from 25% to a peak of 37% in 2004, ranking first that year, then fell before recovering to around 31% in 2012. Meanwhile, that for Belgium climbed from 17% to 28% between 2000 and 2004, after which it remained relatively stable until 2012.

reviews.originalEssay:
The give line chart illustrates the percentages of women in parliament across five European countries between 2000 and 2012
Overall , out of the studied nations , it's clear that the percentages of female representatives in Italy and the UK experienced an upward trend , whereas Germany hardly changed . Moreover , Italy surpassed Germany to become the country with the highest proportion in 2012 , while the UK consistently remained at the lowest position
To elaborate, in 2000, the UK had the lowest percentage of members at only 3%, but it increased steadily to about 27% in 2012. By contrast, Germany started highest at 33% and rose slightly to nearly 37%. Italy saw a big increase from 26% to almost 40%, surpassing Germany in 2012.
Regarding the remaining countries, France and Belgium also went up, ending the period at about 32% and 28% respectively

The bar chart compares the percentages of males and females who participated in eight named sports and an Other category in the United Kingdom in 2008.

Overall, soccer recorded the highest male participation, whereas netball was the most popular sport among females. Netball also had the widest gap between the two groups. Male participation in netball and female participation in cricket were the lowest for their respective groups. Tennis and basketball, by contrast, showed similar figures for both genders.

To elaborate, about 24% of males played soccer, compared with around 5% of females. Cricket was also more common among males, at approximately 10%, while the figure for females was around 1%. The male percentage for table tennis stood at 9%, triple the corresponding female figure of about 3%. In the Other category, the figures were approximately 20% and 10%, respectively.

Regarding sports with higher female participation, about 25% of females played netball, while only around 1% of males did so. Swimming attracted roughly 22% of females, compared with 14% of males. Tennis and basketball each had participation rates of about 6–7% for both genders. Jogging was less common, with around 4% of females and 3% of males participating.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The bar chart compares the yearly salaries of doctors and other workers across seven countries in 2004, measured in thousands of United States dollars.

Overall, doctors earned more than other workers in every country. The United States had the highest pay for both groups and the widest gap between them, while Finnish doctors received the lowest salary among doctors. Other workers earned the least in Italy, the Czech Republic and Germany.

In the United States, doctors earned about $120,000 a year, compared with roughly $46,000 for other workers, a difference of approximately $74,000. Doctors in France and Switzerland each received about $70,000, but the corresponding figures for other workers differed: around $30,000 in France and $40,000 in Switzerland.

The given table chart illustrates the proportion of first-year students who gave an excellent rating to the resources provided by the college for three cources .

Overall , Commerce was the most high rating percentage in most categories , while Law had lower rating . Also of note is that ,Teaching was highly rated by Economics and Commerce students ,whereas Pre-course information gained the lowest score for Economics .

Regarding categories with less pronounced data, other resources received the highest rating, at 80%, followed by tutors at 76%. The figures for pre-course information and printed resources stood at 72% and 70%, respectively.By contrast , Teaching had the lowest proportion in this course, at just 62%, which was considerably lower than the 95% recorded for the other two courses.

reviews.overall: Em đã chia hai đoạn chi tiết theo Law và Business, phù hợp với cách so sánh hai ngành trong biểu đồ. Nhận xét B cao nhất ở Law và C đứng đầu ở Business vẫn đúng khi mức lương cao nhất có đồng hạng. Tuy nhiên, em gọi A thấp nhất ở cả hai số liệu dù lương Law của A bằng B; em cũng nhầm 60 nghìn ở Business C là lương và 50 nghìn ở Business B là mức chênh lệch, trong khi cả hai là học phí. Bài này em soát chưa kỹ. Cô yêu cầu em kiểm lại tên hai đại lượng, từng cặp số và mức chênh lệch trước khi nộp lại.
reviews.dataGrouping: Em đã có bốn đoạn: mở bài, tổng quan, một đoạn về Law và một đoạn về Business. Cách chia theo ngành này hợp lý và được giữ trong bản sửa. Trong mỗi đoạn, em cần ghi rõ đại lượng đang so sánh và tính khoảng chênh lệch từ hai số tương ứng. Overview có thể gọi B cao nhất ở Law và C đứng đầu ở Business: lương của B đồng hạng A, còn lương của C đồng hạng B. Em nên nói rõ điều đó và sửa nhận xét A thấp nhất ở cả hai số liệu, vì lương Law của A không thấp nhất.

The given bar chart illustrates how much students earn income  and pay in university fees at three university in two fields about Law and Business.
Overall ,student of  university B had the highest figures in Law , meanwhile university C ranked first in Business . Conversely , student of university A offer the lowest figures in both fields , while the lowest salaries were recorded at university C in Law and university A in Business.
To elaborate , in the fields of Law ,  student of university B had the highest income and fees , while the second highest in fees is university C . By contrast , student of university A had the same figure was around 40thousand of dollars  and were substantially lower than those of university B and C.
Regarding the fields about Business , student in university C earned salaries the most (60 thousand of dollars ) , whereas the opposite was true in student of university A and B . Student of university B ranked second in Business , with only 50 thousand of dollars lower , this figure was significantly higher than salaries of student in university A . As for the fees , 40 thousand of dollars was recorded in university C higher than the fees in unversity A (30 thousand of dollars).

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The two pie charts illustrate the main reasons why people immigrated to and emigrated from the UK in 2007.

Overall, having a definite job accounted for the largest share in both groups. Formal study was far more common among immigrants and was the least common reason for emigration, whereas looking for work represented a larger share of emigrants than immigrants.

To elaborate, 30% of immigrants already had a definite job, compared with 29% of emigrants. Formal study was the second most common reason for immigration, at 26%, but accounted for only 4% of emigration. Conversely, 22% of emigrants were looking for work, a proportion 10 percentage points higher than the corresponding 12% of immigrants.

Regarding the remaining reasons, 15% of immigrants accompanied or joined someone, compared with 13% of emigrants. No reason was stated for 6% of immigrants, while the corresponding figure for emigrants was 18%. Finally, the Other category accounted for 11% of immigration and 14% of emigration.
